heading: How should I optimize a JPEG camera export?
introduction: Use this page to re-encode a JPEG photograph while keeping original display dimensions by default. JPEG and JPG are the same format, and both pages use the same image engine.

sections.heading: Work from the largest useful source
sections.body: Work from your camera or editor export rather than repeatedly recompressing a previous download. Choose Balanced, High quality, Maximum or a separate Target size, then compare the output at the same scale. Image dimensions are preserved.

sections.heading: Changing an extension does not compress a photograph
sections.body: Renaming .jpeg to .jpg leaves the encoded image data unchanged. Re-encoding changes size and detail, while a higher quality setting cannot recover detail lost earlier. If ordinary same-format compression finds no smaller result, the original file is returned unchanged with 0% reduction.

sections.heading: Check the finished image
sections.body: Review gradients, fine textures, text, dimensions and orientation. Re-encoding may normalize colors to sRGB and remove metadata; a retained original keeps its bytes and metadata. Keep an original for printing or further editing.

seoDescription: Optimize JPEG photographs with browser-based quality controls and preserved dimensions. JPG and JPEG use the same format; review each result.
